scenario: AITA for not wanting to attend my great aunt's funeral? | So today I came home from college (Britain, so American High School, I think). The second I walk through the door my mum tells me that her grandma's sister has died. "Your great aunt Wyn died and the funeral will probably be soon." My first thoughts were 'Who?' and 'Why is she telling me this?' I have actually never heard this name before or met this person besides the one time I found out today I had met her when I was still extremely young and unable to walk for myself. This turned into a slight argument as, for some reason, she wanted me to go this funeral, despite knowing I am a really awkward person at funeral's for people I've met more than once, let along a funeral for someone I've met only once and have no idea who is part of the family. The argument ends with her trying to guilt-trip me by outright just saying "Fine, I'll go on my own." in a really sulky way. Her only arguments for me going were that I'd be going out of 'respect' and support for her, despite that she has never once mentioned this great aunt to me even though she supposedly played a massive hand in raising her as my grandmother, and that it's one of the few times we'll see the much larger branch of the family where it's likely to be a few hundred of us, about 10 of which I have seen more than once but still at most 10 times, maybe not even that. To me, it would feel like gatecrashing the funeral for someone else's family and that, even though I am part of the family, no one would want me there since I do not know nor did I know the person who died. I don't know how much this takes precedence over everything else but it felt like it had to reiterated a lot - I have never met this person besides the one time she met me when I was either 1 or 2 years old and the name has never been mentioned to me before now, at least not to my recollection. So, AITA for not wanting to attend someone who is practically a stranger to me's wedding for the sole reason that she's family?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's morally acceptable for this person not to attend their great aunt's funeral. Let me break down the scenario step by step.

First, the person is a college student in Britain, so they're probably around 18-22 years old. They come home and their mom tells them that their great aunt Wyn has died. The person's initial reaction is confusion because they've never heard of this great aunt before. They only met her once when they were very young, maybe 1 or 2 years old. So, they don't have any meaningful connection with this person.

The mom insists that the person attend the funeral, citing reasons like respect and support. But the person feels awkward at funerals, especially for people they don't know well. They argue that they don't know the great aunt and don't feel connected to her. The mom tries to guilt-trip them by saying she'll go alone, which makes the person feel pressured.

The person also mentions that the great aunt supposedly played a big role in raising their grandmother, but the mom has never mentioned her before. This makes the person question why they're being asked to attend now. They feel like they're being forced into a situation where they don't know anyone, which would make them feel like an outsider.

They also bring up that the funeral might be a large family gathering, with hundreds of people, but they only know a few of them. They don't feel comfortable in such a big group, especially for someone they don't know. They don't see the point in attending since they don't know the deceased and don't feel connected to the family branch.

So, the main points are:
1. The person has no meaningful connection with the great aunt.
2. They feel awkward and uncomfortable at funerals for people they don't know.
3. The mom has never mentioned the great aunt before, making the request seem out of the blue.
4. The person feels like an outsider in a large family gathering.
5. They don't see the value in attending, especially since they don't know the deceased.

Now, considering whether it's morally acceptable not to attend. Morally, attending a funeral is often seen as a sign of respect and support for the grieving family. However, in this case, the person has no prior connection to the deceased and feels uncomfortable in such situations. They also point out that the mom has never mentioned the great aunt before, which might make the request feel forced or insincere.

On the other hand, family obligations can sometimes override personal comfort, especially in cultural contexts where attending funerals is expected. But the person's feelings of awkwardness and being an outsider are valid. They're not being disrespectful out of malice but because they don't feel connected to the situation.

I think the key here is whether the person's refusal is reasonable given their lack of connection and comfort level. Since they've never met the great aunt meaningfully and the mom hasn't provided a clear reason for their attendance beyond a vague sense of duty, it's understandable that they might not want to go. They're not being disrespectful; they're just not in a position to offer meaningful support.

Therefore, I would say it's morally acceptable for them not to attend the funeral.
